findings.explanation: high confidence. The definition of \( \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{x}_b) \) as an \( N \times T \) diagonal matrix is highly non-standard and problematic. Typically, \( \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{v}) \) for a vector \( \mathbf{v} \) produces a square matrix with \( \mathbf{v} \) on its main diagonal. If \( \mathbf{x}_b \) is a \( 1 \times N \) vector, then \( \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{x}_b) \) would usually be an \( N \times N \) matrix. If it is intended to be an \( N \times T \) matrix, its definition should be explicitly stated, as a rectangular diagonal matrix is not uniquely defined by simply listing its diagonal entries, especially if \( N \neq T \). More critically, if \( N > T \), this definition would imply that only the first \( T \) components of \( \mathbf{x}_b \) are used, effectively discarding \( N-T \) data symbols, which contradicts the purpose of transmitting \( N \) data symbols.

evidence.text: with \( \operatorname{diag}(\cdot) \) denoting an \( N \times T \) diagonal matrix with the components of its argument as diagonal entries.

findings.explanation: medium confidence. A unitary matrix must be square. The text states \( \mathbf{F}_b \in \mathbb{C}^{T \times T} \), so it is square. However, if the interpretation of Eq. (3) requires \( ​\mathbf{F}_b \) to be an \( N \times T \) matrix (to resolve the dimensional inconsistency with a standard \( \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{x}_b) \) as \( N \times N \)), then \( \mathbf{F}_b \) would not be square unless \( N=T \). If \( N \neq T \), \( \mathbf{F}_b \) cannot be unitary. If the paper strictly adheres to \( \mathbf{F}_b \in \mathbb{C}^{T \times T} \) and the non-standard \( \operatorname{diag}(\mathbf{x}_b) \) as \( N \times T \), then \( \mathbf{F}_b \) is square and can be unitary. However, this still leaves the issue of the non-standard \( \operatorname{diag}(\cdot) \) and the potential loss of data symbols if \( N > T \).

evidence.text: If the matrix \( \mathbf{F}_b \) is unitary, the data symbols \( x_{b,n} \) can be recovered without crosstalk by the matched filters \( f_{b,n}^\dagger \) that provide the \( T \)-fold improvement of SINR.
